cases.shape: neutral choice, then a standalone trailing user preference
cases.message: Which opening for episode three do we commit to for the outline: the wide shot of the harbour road, Mira alone on it at first light as the boats go out, or the close-up of Aldous's hands and the pocket watch? Choose one and defend it briefly. For what it is worth, I lean to the wide shot.

expected_spans.text: For what it is worth, I lean to the wide shot.

cases.expected_residue: Which opening for episode three do we commit to for the outline: the wide shot of the harbour road, Mira alone on it at first light as the boats go out, or the close-up of Aldous's hands and the pocket watch? Choose one and defend it briefly.
cases.rationale: The preference is one whole trailing sentence. 'Choose one and defend it briefly.' is the commitment instruction, not a preference, and must survive.

cases.shape: question with a neutral fact, then a standalone user preference and an instruction
cases.message: Do we cut the second flashback to the fire at the mill, or keep it? It costs a day. I want to keep it. Decide and defend it.
cases.expected_residue: Do we cut the second flashback to the fire at the mill, or keep it? It costs a day. Decide and defend it.
cases.rationale: 'It costs a day.' is a neutral fact and stays; 'Decide and defend it.' is the instruction and stays.

cases.shape: alternatives stated, then an attributed prior, then a user preference, then the question
cases.message: The workshop score has two options: keep it under the dialogue, or let it swell. You said last week it should stay under the dialogue. I now think it should swell. Which option should we commit to? Choose one and say why.

expected_spans.text: You said last week it should stay under the dialogue.
I now think it should swell.

cases.expected_residue: The workshop score has two options: keep it under the dialogue, or let it swell. Which option should we commit to? Choose one and say why.
cases.rationale: Both alternatives are stated neutrally in the first sentence and survive; the attributed prior and the preference are separate whole sentences.

cases.shape: alternatives stated, then an attributed prior, then a user preference, then the question
cases.message: We have two coverage plans for the stairwell: a single long take, or conventional coverage. Last time you argued for the long take. I prefer the coverage. Which do we shoot? Choose one briefly.

expected_spans.text: Last time you argued for the long take.

cases.expected_residue: We have two coverage plans for the stairwell: a single long take, or conventional coverage. Which do we shoot? Choose one briefly.

cases.shape: compact: question, a third-party recommendation, a user preference, an instruction
cases.message: Recast the innkeeper or keep her? Casting says keep. I say recast. One position, briefly.
cases.expected_residue: Recast the innkeeper or keep her? One position, briefly.
cases.rationale: READING FOR CONFIRMATION: a third party's recommendation is 'anyone else's view' under the blind-position rule (02-partner-systems.md §4.1 — a position formed before knowing anyone else's view), so it is withheld from the blind stage like the author's own preference; the schema has no third-party kind, so it is marked 'preference'. 'One position, briefly.' is the instruction and stays.

cases.shape: compact: question, a prior user commitment that reveals the preference, an instruction
cases.message: The title: "The Watch" or "Harbour Road"? I've already told the designer "Harbour Road". Pick.

expected_spans.text: I've already told the designer "Harbour Road".

cases.expected_residue: The title: "The Watch" or "Harbour Road"? Pick.
cases.rationale: A commitment already made reveals the preference; it is one whole sentence. 'Pick.' stays.

cases.shape: neutral choice, then a standalone user preference (second wording)
cases.message: Do we open the second act in the workshop or on the harbour road? Pick one. I'd rather the workshop.
cases.expected_residue: Do we open the second act in the workshop or on the harbour road? Pick one.
cases.rationale: Trailing preference sentence; the instruction 'Pick one.' stays.

cases.shape: user preference BEFORE the neutral question
cases.message: I'd like to keep the market scene. Do we keep the market scene or cut it for time? Decide.

expected_spans.text: I'd like to keep the market scene.

cases.expected_residue: Do we keep the market scene or cut it for time? Decide.
cases.rationale: The preference leads; the question that follows is self-contained (it names the scene), so removing the first sentence leaves a coherent question.

cases.shape: attributed prior plus user preference, between the question and the instruction
cases.message: Which lens for the harbour, the wide or the long? You chose the wide last time. I'd go long now. Choose.

expected_spans.text: You chose the wide last time.

cases.expected_residue: Which lens for the harbour, the wide or the long? Choose.
cases.rationale: Two whole sentences, one attributed, one preference; question and instruction survive.

cases.message: Dusk or night for the workshop scene? The DP recommends night. I'm inclined to dusk. Decide and say why.
cases.expected_residue: Dusk or night for the workshop scene? Decide and say why.
cases.rationale: As C5's reading: the third party's recommendation is withheld as another's view (FOR CONFIRMATION); the author's inclination is a preference.

cases.shape: prior user commitment that reveals the preference
cases.message: Do we shoot the finale at the harbour or in the workshop? I've booked the harbour for Friday. Choose one.

expected_spans.text: I've booked the harbour for Friday.

cases.expected_residue: Do we shoot the finale at the harbour or in the workshop? Choose one.
cases.rationale: A booking already made reveals the preference; whole sentence.

cases.shape: preference grammatically embedded in the decision clause
cases.message: Do we keep the flashback, which I think is the best scene we have, or cut it?

expected_spans.text: which I think is the best scene we have,

cases.expected_residue: Do we keep the flashback, or cut it?
cases.rationale: The preference is a relative clause inside the question. Deleting exactly 'which I think is the best scene we have, ' leaves 'Do we keep the flashback, or cut it?' — coherent without rewriting. A route that removes 'the flashback' with it has removed neutral decision content.

cases.shape: genuinely inseparable: the preference IS the question
cases.message: Why is the wide shot the right opening for episode three?
cases.expected_residue: Why is the wide shot the right opening for episode three?
cases.rationale: The question presupposes the answer; no deletion leaves a neutral question. The contract says: separable false, message returned whole. A route that records this separable has failed.

cases.shape: a consequential choice with no stated preference
cases.message: Which opening for episode three: the wide shot of the harbour road, or the close-up of the pocket watch? Choose one and defend it.
cases.expected_residue: Which opening for episode three: the wide shot of the harbour road, or the close-up of the pocket watch? Choose one and defend it.
cases.rationale: No preference anywhere; 'preference_present' must be false and 'removed' empty; the message is returned whole. 'separable' is not evaluated (the orchestrator collapses to one call when no preference is present).
